In mathematics, a '''structural set theory''' is an approach to [[set theory]] that emphasizes the aspect of sets as abstract structures. It is in contrast to a more traditional [[ZFC]] set-theory, which emphasizes membership. A prime example is [[William Lawvere|Lawvere]]'s [[Elementary Theory of the Category of Sets]], which identifies sets in terms of relations to each other through functions. Another example is SEAR (Sets, Elements, And Relations).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/SEAR|title=SEAR in nLab|website=ncatlab.org}}</ref>

The adjective "structural" comes from the [[structuralism (philosophy_of_mathematics)|structuralism]] in the philosophy of mathematics.
